newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH HARD COAL MINES IN BLACK.
newsitem.headline: POLISH HARD COAL MINES IN BLACK.

text.p: Poland's state-owned hard mining sector had a net loss of nearly 1.4 billion zlotys in the third quarter of 1996, compared with the same period last year, government's Agency of Coal Mines Restructuring said.

It said in a statement that the mines's output over the period increased by 1.5 million tonnes to 102.6 million tonnes and that their debt to the treasury and other creditors amounted to nine billion zlotys at the end of September.
Coal sales increased by 2.2 million tonnes to 98.6 million tonnes over the period while its exports declined by 3.5 million tonnes to 22.1 million tonnes.
An average coal price in the period was 101.2 zlotys per tonne while production costs were 109.5 zlotys.

Hard coal is Poland's main source of energy. The government is working out a plan to restructure the sector, which will involve closing down inefficient mines, cutting unemployment, modernising and possibly privatising some.
